speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, Patrick, thanks so much for being here.
zh: 好的，Patrick，非常感谢你能来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome to Startup School.
zh: 欢迎来到 Startup School。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great to be here.
zh: 很高兴来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Harge and I first met 20 years ago, and we started a company together.
zh: Harge 和我 20 年前第一次见面，然后我们一起创办了一家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sorry, am I giving away the introduction?
zh: 抱歉，我是不是把介绍环节给抢了？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I thought this was my interview, but sure.
zh: 是啊，我本来以为这是我的访谈，不过行吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Keep going.
zh: 你继续说。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're doing a good job.
zh: 你做得挺好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We started a company together many, many years ago, and I learned a huge amount from Harge.
zh: 很多年前我们一起创办了一家公司，我从 Harge 身上学到了非常多的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's really fun to do this.
zh: 所以能来做这个节目真的很开心。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, actually, I mean, speaking of that, so I think when I first met you 20-something-ish years ago, at the time, your most impressive achievement, I would argue, was Chroma, your dialect of Lisp.
zh: 嗯，其实，我是说，说到这个，我记得 20 多年前我第一次见到你的时候，你当时最令人印象深刻的成就，我认为，是 Chroma，你的那个 Lisp 方言。

speaker: Unknown
en: Any Lisp programmers here?
zh: 这里有 Lisp 程序员吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, wow.
zh: 哦，哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was, I think I heard one whoop, which is more than I expected.
zh: 我好像听到了一声欢呼，这已经超出我的预期了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, I really liked Lisp when I was in high school.
zh: 不过是的，我高中的时候真的很喜欢 Lisp。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what I was going to ask is a prolific 16-year-old today could presumably just prompt Claude to write their Lisp dialect.
zh: 所以我本来想问的是，今天一个多产的 16 岁少年，大概可以直接让 Claude 去写他们的 Lisp 方言。

speaker: Unknown
en: Would you advise them to not do that and still do it?
zh: 你会建议他们不要那么做、还是依然自己动手做？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there any value in such things?
zh: 这类事情还有价值吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know.
zh: 我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wonder a lot.
zh: 我经常在想这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, like obviously on the one hand, it used to be really fun to write all this assembly and machine code and to optimize your instructions and layout and memory and everything.
zh: 嗯，比如显然一方面，过去写汇编和机器码、优化你的指令、内存布局什么的，真的很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now we don't have to do that anymore.
zh: 而现在我们不再需要那么做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our compilers do it for us.
zh: 我们的编译器替我们做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't mourn it too much.
zh: 我们也没有太为此哀悼。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so maybe in the same way, we shouldn't mourn source code.
zh: 所以也许同样地，我们不应该哀悼源代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: We should just transcend the plane of instructions to Claudius et al.
zh: 我们应该直接超越到指令这一层之上，交给 Claude 之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But emotionally, I miss it.
zh: 但从情感上讲，我怀念它。

speaker: Unknown
en: How about, I think, just as I've been hanging out here with these students, maybe the question behind it is many of them are just wondering, what should they be learning at college?
zh: 要不要这样，我想，既然我一直在和这些学生待在一起，也许这背后的问题是，他们中的很多人都在想，大学里应该学什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is in this AI world?
zh: 在这个 AI 世界里？

speaker: Unknown
en: How much should they be trying to learn and derive from first principles, and how much should they just outsource to the AI?
zh: 他们应该花多少力气去学习、从第一性原理去推导，又应该把多少外包给 AI？

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, my model of this is...
zh: 我是说，我对这个的理解是……

speaker: Unknown
en: is cache, you know, the CH, not an SH, where Jeff Dean has this famous set of numbers that every programmer should know, bandwidths and latencies and just kind of relevant constants that you show the reason about as you build systems.
zh: 是缓存，你知道的，是 CH 开头不是 SH 开头，Jeff Dean 有一组著名的数字，每个程序员都该知道，就是各种带宽和延迟，以及一些相关的常数，你构建系统时会参考它们来推理。

speaker: Unknown
en: And obviously, when you're thinking of building any system or distributed system or whatever, like all lookups and all relevant bandwidths between different
zh: 显然，当你在考虑构建任何系统、分布式系统之类的东西时，所有的查找以及不同

speaker: Unknown
en: Components are very different, right?
zh: 组件之间的相关带宽都差别很大，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And retrieving something from L1 cache is very different.
zh: 从 L1 缓存取东西是非常不一样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Retrieving from RAM is very different from retrieving across the network or whatever.
zh: 从 RAM 里取，和跨网络取，或者其他方式，差别非常大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's like that with knowledge.
zh: 而我认为知识也是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're fine.
zh: 我们没事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, you can ask the agent or something to compute something for you or to look something up for you, whatever.
zh: 是的，你可以让智能体帮你算点什么，或者帮你查点什么，诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a hell of a lot slower than knowing it in cognitive L1 cache.
zh: 但那比在你认知的 L1 缓存里直接知道它要慢得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can have way more round trips in your brain than you can
zh: 而且你大脑里能做的往返次数，远远多于

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, muttering through, you know, SuperWhisper or typing it out or whatever.
zh: 你知道的，通过 SuperWhisper 念出来或者打字打出来之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think even granting the full capabilities of the models, I still think there's a pretty, like, I think for a long time to come, neuronal lookups will be much faster.
zh: 所以我认为，即便完全承认模型的能力，我仍然觉得，在相当长的一段时间里，神经元查找会快得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, look, if you look in revealed preference at what companies themselves are doing, whether they're companies like Stripe or The Labs or what have you, there still seems to be an enormous premium on cognitive ability.
zh: 然后，你看，如果你从显示性偏好去看这些公司自己正在做什么，无论是像 Stripe 这样的公司还是那些实验室之类的，认知能力仍然享有巨大的溢价。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think renouncing that before there is evidence that we've saturated those benefits would be premature.
zh: 所以我认为，在还没有证据表明这些收益已经被榨干之前，就放弃认知能力会是为时过早的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are there specific things that maybe you personally, either personally or as CEO of Stripe, you still purposely choose to do yourself and retrieve from your own cache, even though the agents would probably do a reasonably good job?
zh: 有没有什么具体的事情，也许你个人，无论是作为个人还是作为 Stripe 的 CEO，你仍然刻意选择自己去做、从自己的缓存里检索的，尽管智能体大概也能做得相当不错？

speaker: Unknown
en: I still write myself.
zh: 我至今仍然自己写作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't...
zh: 我不……

speaker: Unknown
en: I both philosophically, but also specifically, substantively, dislike the writing of the models.
zh: 无论是哲学层面,还是具体、实质的层面,我都不喜欢模型的写作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's very interesting, right, because these can prove the Jacobian conjecture, you know, whatever.
zh: 我是说,这很有意思,对吧,因为它们能证明雅可比猜想,什么的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so clearly they're capable of these monumental feats.
zh: 所以很显然,它们有能力完成这些非凡的壮举。

speaker: Unknown
en: But somehow I still haven't read the LLM essay that I found super compelling.
zh: 但不知为何,我至今还没读到过让我觉得非常有说服力的 LLM 文章。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, I think it's just very hard to, like, RL limit that domain because the, you know, the...
zh: 现在,我认为这很难,比如说,很难在这个领域上 RL 限制,因为,你知道,那个……

speaker: Unknown
en: Utility function or something is kind of hard to define.
zh: 效用函数之类的,很难定义。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, I think writing is a pretty... Interpersonal communication and writing I think are still very fundamental and sort of being able to reason sensibly in the multidimensional space of reality.
zh: 但是的,我觉得写作还是相当……人际沟通和写作我认为仍然非常根本,以及在现实的多维空间中进行合理推理的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in some kind of indescribable way, I feel like the model is still kind of deficient at that.
zh: 而且以某种难以描述的方式,我觉得模型在那方面仍然有点欠缺。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I've never...
zh: 所以我从来没有……

speaker: Unknown
en: I've yet to send, you know...
zh: 我至今还没发送过,你知道……

speaker: Unknown
en: Every tool is now trying to prompt me with pre-written suggestions, whether it's Gmail or apparently WhatsApp just rolled this out.
zh: 现在每个工具都在尝试用预先写好的建议来提示我,无论是 Gmail,还是显然 WhatsApp 也刚刚推出了这个功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think I've still sent zero of those in my life.
zh: 而且我想我这一辈子一条都没发过。

speaker: Unknown
en: How about if you talk about the Stripe story, the early days in particular, a little bit.
zh: 你能稍微谈谈 Stripe 的故事吗,尤其是早期?

speaker: Unknown
en: You were at MIT, then you left to start Stripe.
zh: 你在 MIT,然后你离开去创办了 Stripe。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you think about that decision?
zh: 你当时是怎么考虑那个决定的?

speaker: Unknown
en: And obviously, we're in a stadium full of college students.
zh: 显然,我们现在在一个坐满大学生的体育馆里。

speaker: Unknown
en: How should they think about it?
zh: 他们应该怎么考虑这件事?

speaker: Unknown
en: How do they know if it's the right decision for them to leave college early and go start a company versus stay?
zh: 他们怎么知道提早离开大学去创业对他们来说是不是正确的决定,还是留下来?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, well, I think I have the slightly unusual distinction of having dropped out of college twice to start a company.
zh: 是的,我想我有一个稍微不寻常的独特之处,就是我为了创业两次从大学辍学。

speaker: Unknown
en: So maybe one thing to know is that it's not totally trapdoor.
zh: 所以也许有一点需要知道的是,这并不是完全的活板门。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can drop out and, in fact, return.
zh: 你可以辍学,而且实际上,还可以回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I dropped out after my freshman semester.
zh: 所以我在大一学期之后就辍学了。

speaker: Unknown
en: to start this company with Harge.
zh: 去和 Harge 一起创办那家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was super fun.
zh: 那非常有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then after a couple of years of that, went back, did another year at MIT, and then dropped out again to start Stripe.
zh: 然后在做了几年之后,我回去,在 MIT 又读了一年,然后再次辍学去创办 Stripe。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when I went to college, probably like a lot of people here, I...
zh: 而我上大学的时候,大概和在座很多人一样,我……

speaker: Unknown
en: I had this vision of my life involving becoming an academic.
zh: 我有过这样的人生愿景,就是成为一名学者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I really liked physics.
zh: 而且我非常喜欢物理。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I thought, you know, I'll do all this physics stuff.
zh: 我想,你知道,我会做所有这些物理相关的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's so cool.
zh: 太酷了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd read all the Feynman books, all of this.
zh: 我读过所有的 Feynman 书籍,诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I guess I am, well, growing up in Ireland, I hadn't thought much about the possibility of startups.
zh: 而我想,我在爱尔兰长大,我之前没怎么想过创业的可能性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hello to the other Irish folks here.
zh: 向这里的其他爱尔兰朋友们问好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And way back then, in the sort of pre-Cambrian era, startups were definitely much less well-known, even on campus and so forth.
zh: 而在很久以前,在那个类似前寒武纪的时代,创业公司肯定没有那么为人所知,即使在校园里等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I was dropping out, people thought it was super weird.
zh: 当我辍学时,人们觉得这非常奇怪。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think overall,
zh: 我认为总体来说,

speaker: Unknown
en: If you enjoy college, I would actually, you know, I think there's no harm in finishing.
zh: 如果你享受大学生活,我实际上,你知道,我认为读完没有任何坏处。

speaker: Unknown
en: I felt this real sense of urgency, which I think in hindsight was a bit unnecessary.
zh: 我当时有一种真切的紧迫感,现在回想起来,我觉得那有点不必要。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you don't enjoy college, just, you know, whatever, it's not your thing.
zh: 但如果你不享受大学生活,那就,你知道,无所谓,它不是你的菜。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not what captivates you.
zh: 它不是让你着迷的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't really want to learn all the physics things or whatever.
zh: 你并不真的想学所有的物理知识之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think a lot of parents think that dropping out is very risky and will impugn your reputation for the rest of your life and so forth.
zh: 是的,我想很多父母认为辍学风险很大,会损害你一辈子的名誉等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as far as I can tell, nobody has ever cared.
zh: 而据我所知,从来没有人真正在意过。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I both think you don't need to, but also the cost of doing so are de minimis.
zh: 所以我既认为你不需要这样做,同时也认为这样做的成本微乎其微。

speaker: Unknown
en: What was the urgency you were feeling?
zh: 你当时感受到的紧迫感是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: The urgency?
zh: 紧迫感?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, to go out and do something.
zh: 是的,走出去做点什么的紧迫感。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know.
zh: 我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Life is short, right?
zh: 人生苦短，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I mean, it was a general kind of haste.
zh: 我是说，那是一种总体上的匆忙。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot of us, I'm sure many of the people here, you kind of get into this mode of speed running high school.
zh: 我想我们很多人，我相信在场的很多人，都会有某种类似速通高中的模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then once you get to college, it's like, obviously, I want to speed run that as well and do all the things.
zh: 然后一旦上了大学，就好像，显然，我也想速通大学，做完所有的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's a bit of that, a bit of...
zh: 所以有一部分是这个原因，还有一部分是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Marc Andreessen also talks about a version of this.
zh: Marc Andreessen 也谈到过类似的观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought that a bunch of the opportunities in startups and in Silicon Valley and so forth were ephemeral and fleeting.
zh: 我当时认为创业、硅谷等等领域里的很多机会都是短暂的、转瞬即逝的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we didn't build it then, it wouldn't be possible to do it in three or four years.
zh: 如果我们那时不把它做出来，三四年之后就不可能再做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And maybe all the opportunities will be gone.
zh: 也许所有的机会都会消失。

speaker: Unknown
en: In hindsight, I think that was a poor intuition.
zh: 事后来看，我觉得那是一种很糟糕的直觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been pretty robustly and reliably the case over many decades that Silicon Valley has a surfeit of opportunities.
zh: 几十年来，硅谷一直相当稳固且可靠地存在着过剩的机会，这一点一直如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think it was mainly those two things.
zh: 是的，我想主要是这两件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think it's, I mean, this is a very common thing that we hear when we talk to students now, is that they are, part of the reason they want to drop out en masse, it seems at this point, is their worry that actually now is the moment that there's sort of, I think the meme going around is that if you don't sort of drop out and start a company and make lots of money, you're going to be trapped in the permanent underclass.
zh: 你觉得这是不是……我是说，这是我们现在和学生交流时经常听到的事情，就是他们大规模想辍学的原因之一，至少现在看起来是这样，是担心现在实际上正是那个时刻，我记得流传的一个梗是，如果你不辍学去创业、赚大钱，你就会被困在永久底层阶级里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So is that, should everyone here be worried about being stuck in the permanent underclass, I guess is the question.
zh: 所以在座的各位是否都应该担心被困在永久底层阶级里，我想这就是问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think humanity has always had an affinity for these millenarian models of how everything will soon come to an end and be this sort of...
zh: 我认为人类一直以来都对这类千年至福论式的模式情有独钟，认为一切都将很快终结，变成某种……

speaker: Unknown
en: Permanent transformation of society and so forth.
zh: 社会的永久性转型等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, there's a great book, The Winged Gospel.
zh: 实际上有一本很棒的书，叫 The Winged Gospel（《带翅膀的福音》）。

speaker: Unknown
en: People thought that after the invention of aviation, that it was just, like, civilization was just entering, and humanity as a species were entering a new era, and nothing is going to be the same.
zh: 人们曾认为，在航空发明之后，就像是，文明正在进入、人类作为一个物种正在进入一个新时代，一切都将会不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, obviously, aviation was...
zh: 显然，航空确实……

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a pretty big deal, but I don't think it was quite the sociological rewriting that some of the excitable proponents at the time imagined.
zh: 它确实是件大事，但我不认为它达到了当时那些亢奋的支持者所想象的那种社会学层面的彻底重写。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's hard to predict anything, especially in the future, but I would take the under on this being the last couple of years to create a company.
zh: 所以预测任何事情都很难，尤其是预测未来，但对于“这是创建公司的最后几年窗口”这一点，我倾向于低估。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fair enough.
zh: 有道理。

speaker: Unknown
en: So going back to the Stripe story, Stripe ostensibly seems like a good idea.
zh: 回到 Stripe 的故事，Stripe 表面上看起来是个好主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like even on day one, the Internet's a big deal, money's a big deal, like combine those two things.
zh: 甚至在第一天，互联网是件大事，钱是件大事，把这两件事结合起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Presumably, is that how it went when you went to tell people you wanted to start Stripe and everyone would just say, hey, this is obviously a good idea?
zh: 那么据推测，当你去告诉别人你想创办 Stripe 时，是不是每个人都直接说，嘿，这显然是个好主意？

speaker: Unknown
en: It was kind of funny.
zh: 那其实挺有意思的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was something we learned from YC was that the importance of focusing on very concrete, easy to explain customer problems.
zh: 这是我们从 YC 学到的东西之一：专注于非常具体、容易解释的客户问题的重要性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like it's very easy to hallucinate or to imagine some customer problem that's not actually something viscerally felt by a person who would pay money.
zh: 因为很容易凭空想象出某个客户问题，而它实际上并不是一个真正愿意付钱的人切身感受到的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so over the course of, in part, working on Automatic together, we have encountered this issue of it being really annoying to deal with.
zh: 所以在一段时间里，部分是在一起做 Automatic 的过程中，我们遇到了这个问题：在互联网上处理资金转移、支付之类的事情真的很烦人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Movement of money or payments or whatever on the internet.
zh: 比如钱的流动、支付，诸如此类，在互联网上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And on the one hand, it seemed like an obviously good idea in the sense that nobody liked the existing ways of doing so.
zh: 一方面，它看起来显然是个好主意，因为没有人喜欢现有的做法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they were broadly extremely unpopular and kind of antiquated and legacy and yet to like fill out this paperwork and go to the bank in person and the paperwork was in Latin and just like it was all bad.
zh: 那些方式普遍极其不受欢迎，而且有点过时、老旧，还得填写各种纸质文件、亲自去银行，文件还是拉丁文写的，总之全都很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then the flip side is it just seems kind of ridiculous that two kids would start a financial services business.
zh: 但反过来说，两个小孩要创办一家金融服务企业，这看起来就有点荒谬。

speaker: Unknown
en: And fintech didn't exist as a sector at the time.
zh: 而且当时金融科技（fintech）作为一个行业还不存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, the word literally didn't exist.
zh: 这个词当时根本不存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's just kind of, you know, we felt like the proverbial squirrels, you know, in a trench coat trying to masquerade as a sort of a real business or as, you know, serious adults, but obviously knowing nothing coming in about the
zh: 所以就感觉，你知道，我们就像那些穿着风衣假扮生意的松鼠，你知道的，试图伪装成一家正经的企业，或者，你知道的，假装成严肃的成年人，但显然我们对这一行一无所知，什么都不懂就进场了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And certainly a lot of people we met and pitched or banks or partners or whatever that we talked to, I mean, they didn't literally laugh us out of the room, but you kind of see them looking for the button to, like, call security under the desk and have them haul us out because it just seems so improbable.
zh: 当然，我们见过的很多人、去 pitch 过的人、或者我们交谈过的银行或合作伙伴之类的，我是说，他们没有真的把我们赶出房间，但你能看到他们在桌子底下找按钮，想叫保安把我们拖出去，因为这一切看起来太不可能了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So anyway, I'd say it both seemed like an obviously good idea in that people really wanted this, but also a bad idea in that nobody took us seriously.
zh: 所以总之，我想说，它一方面显然是个好主意，因为人们确实很需要这个；但另一方面又是个坏主意，因为没人把我们当回事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think the fact that it was, ultimately, the fact that it was grounded in such a concrete, actual, real user problem saved us.
zh: 但我认为，最终，它扎根于一个非常具体、真实、实在的用户问题，这个事实拯救了我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Speaking of that, in order to actually build the product, you had to get a banking partner and do things that a typical software company did not have to do.
zh: 说到这个，为了真正把产品做出来，你们必须找到一个银行合作伙伴，做一些典型的软件公司不需要做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: As two young founders, how did you manage to convince a bank to trust you in the end?
zh: 作为两位年轻的创始人，你们最终是怎么说服一家银行信任你们的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 嗯。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, actually, this is not an answer to your question.
zh: 其实，这不是在回答你的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: But just the thing that strikes me as I sit here is the reason we decided to start Stripe is because John and I were in college together.
zh: 但我坐在这里时让我印象深刻的一件事是，我们决定创办 Stripe 的原因，是因为 John 和我一起上大学。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was in his freshman year.
zh: 他当时在读大一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we went to startup school in 2009, which was held in Berkeley.
zh: 我们在 2009 年参加了 startup school，那是在伯克利举办的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we thought it was pretty cool.
zh: 我们觉得挺酷的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we went and we got sushi afterwards in Potrero.
zh: 于是活动结束后我们去 Potrero 吃了寿司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we were walking back from sushi.
zh: 我们吃完寿司走回来的路上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're like, you know, we've kind of been kicking around this idea for a payments thing or like we've been thinking of the space.
zh: 我们说，你知道，我们其实一直在琢磨一个支付方向的东西的想法，或者说我一直在思考这个领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was walking back that evening after startup school that we decided to start Stripe.
zh: 就是在那个创业学校活动当晚走回去的路上,我们决定创办 Stripe。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember literally where we were on the road.
zh: 我记得我们当时就在路上的具体位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember what we said to each other, which was, yeah, you know, we might as well, because it probably won't be that hard.
zh: 我记得我们对彼此说的话,大意是:好吧,你知道,我们不妨做做看,因为这大概不会太难。

speaker: Unknown
en: OK.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So moral of the story is go get sushi in Potrero tonight and you might start the next stripe.
zh: 所以这个故事的寓意是:今晚去 Potrero 吃个寿司,你也许就能创办下一个 Stripe。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yes, beware of sort of these ultimate yak shaves.
zh: 是的,要小心这类终极的 yak shave(无止境的前置任务)。

speaker: Unknown
en: We thought we could do it on the side, violin college, you know, take a couple months, and that was almost 17 years ago.
zh: 我们当时以为可以顺手做做,像小提琴课一样,花几个月就行,而那已经是将近 17 年前的事了。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the time, I remember you were also unusual in that you took sort of longer to do a big public launch.
zh: 我记得当时你还很不寻常的一点是,你花了比较长的时间才做一个大型的公开发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: And especially within the YC world, the motto is very much sort of launch early, launch quickly, be out there and iterate.
zh: 尤其是在 YC 的圈子里,信条非常明确,就是要尽早发布、快速发布、走出去并快速迭代。

speaker: Unknown
en: Could you maybe talk us through a little bit about that?
zh: 你能不能稍微讲讲这件事?

speaker: Unknown
en: Why did you do it that way?
zh: 你们为什么那样做?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so we started working on Stripe kind of seriously in the, well, we started working the week after that startup school, but we were kind of in college, wasn't full-time.
zh: 好的,我们大约是在那次创业学校之后开始认真做 Stripe 的,嗯,我们在那之后一周就开始动手了,但我们当时还在上大学,不是全职。

speaker: Unknown
en: We started working full-time the summer of 2010.
zh: 我们 2010 年夏天开始全职做。

speaker: Unknown
en: We launched publicly September 2011, so almost two years after like the first lines of code after the repo was started.
zh: 我们 2011 年 9 月公开发布,距离写下第一批代码、仓库创建差不多快两年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, waiting two years to launch seems, I mean, if we're going to YC meetings every week, I think we'd have bludgeoned on the head.
zh: 是啊,等两年才发布,我的意思是,如果我们每周都去参加 YC 会议,我想我们会被敲脑袋的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in many domains, that probably is the wrong thing to do.
zh: 我想在很多领域,那很可能是错误的做法。

speaker: Unknown
en: In our domain, to come up to your last question, because we had to do so much stuff around security and partners and money movement and infrastructure and reliability and all the things, we didn't feel like we could scale a really good self-serve experience without getting a lot of the preconditions and the infrastructure in place.
zh: 而在我们的领域,回到你上一个问题,因为我们要处理太多与安全、合作伙伴、资金流转、基础设施、可靠性等等相关的事情,我们觉得,如果不把很多前置条件和基础设施准备好,我们没法扩展出一个真正好的自助服务体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the thing that saved us and meant that it wasn't a total walk in the wilderness is we had production users almost from the very beginning.
zh: 我想拯救我们、让我们不至于完全在荒野中摸索的,是我们几乎从一开始就有生产环境的用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: So first lines of code,
zh: 所以第一批代码写下之后,

speaker: Unknown
en: In fall of 09, we got our first live production user in January of 2010.
zh: 09 年秋天,我们在 2010 年 1 月迎来了第一个线上的生产用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like two months into working or whatever.
zh: 也就是说,做了大概两个月左右。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it did very little.
zh: 而且它功能非常少。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like it was very larval and incomplete.
zh: 就是很初步、很不完整。

speaker: Unknown
en: And our first production customer was Ross Boucher at a company called 280 North.
zh: 我们第一个生产客户是一家叫 280 North 公司的 Ross Boucher。

speaker: Unknown
en: And all it could do was charge a card.
zh: 那时候它唯一能做的就是刷一张卡扣款。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so Ross would charge the card.
zh: 所以 Ross 会刷那张卡。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he would ask a reasonable question like, how can I look at all my charges?
zh: 然后他会问一些合理的问题,比如:我怎么查看我所有的扣款记录?

speaker: Unknown
en: And like, reasonable request.
zh: 这是个合理的需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so let's put up a little dashboard here.
zh: 那我们就搭一个简单的小仪表盘。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then he'd be like, well, I want to refund a payment.
zh: 然后他会说:嗯,我想退款一笔付款。

speaker: Unknown
en: And all right, we'll build refund support.
zh: 好吧,那我们就做退款功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then after a couple of weeks, he was like, at some point, do I get my money?
zh: 过了几个星期,他说:那到什么时候我能拿到我的钱?

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're like, hmm, also a reasonable request.
zh: 我们说:嗯,这也是个合理的需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's build that functionality.
zh: 那我们就把这个功能做出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was very kind of just-in-time development.
zh: 所以那是非常「即时按需」的开发方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anyway, so we had a production customer from very early.
zh: 总之,我们在非常早期就有了一个生产客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we did increase, it was in private beta, we increased the number of customers every single month, all the way to that public launch.
zh: 然后我们确实在增长,当时处于内测阶段,我们每个月都在增加客户数量,一直持续到公开发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so every week, we had actual customer feedback requests.
zh: 所以每一周,我们都有真实客户的反馈和需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: New users coming in.
zh: 新用户不断进来。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're learning things from reality as opposed to our own hypothesized or extrapolated conception of it.
zh: 我们是从现实中学习东西,而不是基于我们自己假设的或外推的构想。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think if you have a significant stream like that of grounding, I think it's probably OK to not be like, launch, launch.
zh: 我想如果你有这样一条重要的、能把人拉回现实的反馈流,那么不老是喊着「发布、发布」大概也没问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you're an expert YC partner.
zh: 我是说,你可是经验丰富的 YC 合伙人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you agree?
zh: 你同意吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a good question.
zh: 这是个好问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, it is, this is the issue with advice in general is it's sort of so generalized and like, especially in startups, the exception proves the rule, right?
zh: 嗯,是的,这就是一般性建议普遍存在的问题,它太泛化了,而且尤其在创业领域,例外证明了规则的存在,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think those are, yeah, certainly if, you know, the cost of failure is high, then it almost certainly you have to sort of take longer to like build.
zh: 所以我觉得,是的,当然,你知道,如果失败的代价很高,那你几乎肯定得花更长的时间去构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe a slight tangent, but something I'm curious about related to this though is
zh: 可能稍微跑题一点,但与此相关、我很好奇的一件事是

speaker: Unknown
en: With these coding agents, the ability to just build and produce software cheaply and quickly.
zh: 有了这些编程智能体,能够便宜且快速地构建和产出软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wonder, should people be taking more of this path?
zh: 我在想,人们是不是应该更多地走这条路?

speaker: Unknown
en: Should people be more ambitious in general with what the version one of the thing that they launch is?
zh: 人们在总体上,对于所发布产品的第一版,是不是应该更有雄心一些?

speaker: Unknown
en: Or is it still fundamentally good product design to start narrow and focus and then expand out once you know what people want?
zh: 还是说，先从窄处切入、专注，然后在你了解人们想要什么之后再向外扩张，从根本上说仍是好的产品设计？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a good question.
zh: 这是个好问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think probably in the era of AI.
zh: 我认为在 AI 时代可能确实如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I don't know.
zh: 我是说，我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to some extent, YC will be, I think, the expert here.
zh: 而且在某种程度上，我想 YC 会是这方面的专家。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the whole kind of traditional lean startup doctrine of exactly what you say, like start out by buying the Google ads or something and identify this crevice or whatever and iteratively expand out from it.
zh: 但那种传统的精益创业信条——正如你所说的，比如先买 Google 广告什么的，找到那条缝隙之类的，然后从那里迭代式地向外扩张——

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you can certainly imagine that that becomes much more competitive and much more aggressively tilled, and it's kind of hard to find those little niches.
zh: 我觉得你完全可以想象，那会变得竞争激烈得多、被更激进地开垦，要找到那些小众利基有点难。

speaker: Unknown
en: The internet's a much bigger place than it was 20 years ago when some of those ideas emerged, whereas taking these really divergent starting points where nobody else is trying to
zh: 互联网比 20 年前那些理念诞生时要大得多，而选择这些非常独特的起点，没有其他人试图去

speaker: Unknown
en: Occupy that territory is maybe a more, like, maybe you have to more aggressively decorrelate in the era of AI.
zh: 占领那片领地，也许是一种更……也许在 AI 时代你必须更激进地去相关化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it is interesting to think about, you know, many of the companies that are most successful over the last 10 years, so many of them are very anti-lean startup, right?
zh: 而且我觉得，想想这一点很有意思，你知道，过去 10 年里最成功的那些公司，其中很多都是非常反精益创业的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Whether it's, you know, the labs themselves or Anduril or...
zh: 当然，做商业和金融服务，会有各种各样更深奥、更庞大的类似版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can go down the list.
zh: 你可以一路列下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of them have this characteristic.
zh: 它们很多都有这个特点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe a better way of saying it is 20 years ago, the whole lean startup thing was almost the only thing to do because of capital available and you didn't have AI that made spinning up an organization with many different potentialities and capabilities so much easier.
zh: 也许更好的说法是：20 年前，整个精益创业那套几乎是唯一可做的事，因为可用的资本有限，而且那时没有 AI，让创办一个拥有多种潜在可能和能力的组织变得容易得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whereas now, I think you can start these much more aggressive and ambitious things up front.
zh: 而现在，我觉得你可以一开始就启动这些更激进、更有雄心的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Within sort of YC and probably startup role at this point, you're famous for the, at least the Paul Graham term, schlep blindness, the stripe, at least on the surface was not like, you know, involved a lot of schleps, like things I presume you weren't like the intellectually most interesting things to work on.
zh: 在 YC 内部，以及大概在这个创业圈子里，你以——至少以 Paul Graham 的说法——schlep blindness(苦差盲)而闻名，Stripe 至少表面上并不像……你知道，涉及很多苦差事，比如我猜那些并不是智力上最有意思的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I always found that especially interesting for you because you just mentioned you had academic interest in physics and I just like clearly like, you know, a deep intellectual and have very many things that you're interested in.
zh: 我一直觉得这一点对你来说尤其有意思，因为你刚刚提到你对物理有学术兴趣，而且你显然……你知道，是个很深的思想者，对很多事情都感兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: As Stripe has grown in this big company, in what ways are there intellectual rewards that you've given up and which ones have you gained?
zh: 随着 Stripe 成长为这家大公司，你放弃了哪些智识上的回报，又获得了哪些？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, look, in any company, there's a bunch of stuff that's not that rewarding or in and of itself all that interesting, like setting up payroll.
zh: 是的，你看，在任何公司里，都有一堆事情本身并没有那么有回报，也没那么有意思，比如设置工资发放系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: No one sort of starts a company so that you can set up payroll.
zh: 没有人创办公司是为了设置工资发放。

speaker: Unknown
en: And certainly building business and financial services, there's all sorts of more arcane and extensive versions of that.
zh: 当然,在构建商业和金融服务时,还有各种更深奥、更复杂的版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that I actually feel extremely lucky with Stripe in this respect.
zh: 我觉得在这方面，有 Stripe 我真的感到非常幸运。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think this is something, I don't know if you need to think about it that much up front, but I think one should think about it maybe before you raise a significant amount of money.
zh: 我觉得这是一件……我不知道你是否需要在一开始就多加考虑，但我想你也许应该在融一大笔钱之前想一想。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, you always worry naturally about possibility of failure and, you know, what'll happen if you fail and how to mitigate and avoid failure and all those things.
zh: 你知道，你自然会担心失败的可能性，担心如果你失败了会怎样，以及如何缓解和避免失败等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you need to ask the sort of converse of that, what if you succeed?
zh: 我觉得你需要问这个问题的反面：如果你成功了呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, you raise money and you have customers and you have employees and a whole thing.
zh: 你融了钱，有了客户，有了员工，有了一整套东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, are you going to enjoy that?
zh: 你会享受那样吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you going to want to work on that for 10 years, for 17 years, for 30 years?
zh: 你会想在上面工作 10 年、17 年、30 年吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, Larry Ellison at Oracle is going for, I mean, I guess it'll be a half century soon, right?
zh: 我是说，Oracle 的 Larry Ellison 一直在干，我猜很快就要半个世纪了，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, what if you succeed?
zh: 所以，你知道，如果你成功了呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: And in the case of Stripe...
zh: 就 Stripe 而言……

speaker: Unknown
en: I really love it because we're working with the world's most interesting and innovative companies.
zh: 我真的很热爱它，因为我们在和世界上最有趣、最具创新性的公司合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: 25% of all Delaware corporations are started with Stripe via Atlas, and then we get to partner with them and work with them and hear from them and get their feedback and get the request and everything through the entirety of the journey up to being the Shopify's and the OpenAI's and all the...
zh: 25% 的特拉华州注册公司是通过 Stripe 的 Atlas 创立的，然后我们得以与它们合作、共事、听取它们的意见、获得它们的反馈和需求，贯穿它们成为 Shopify、OpenAI 等等的整个历程……

speaker: Unknown
en: The standout successes.
zh: 那些杰出的成功者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, and actually, speaking of Atlas, we're giving free Atlas incorporation to everybody at Startup School.
zh: 哦，对了，说到 Atlas，我们要为 Startup School 的所有人提供免费的 Atlas 注册服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you are struck by the urge to found something over dinner this evening, as we were, just email startupschool at stripe.com, and we will get you your link for free antlers.
zh: 如果你今晚在晚餐时突然有了创办点什么的冲动——就像我们当年那样——只要发邮件到 startupschool at stripe.com，我们就会把免费注册的链接发给你。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, I think PG latched onto something where, yeah, there are all these menial tasks, but in the totality of Stripe, I find it so...
zh: 不过是的，我觉得 PG 确实抓住了某个东西，是的，有所有这些琐碎的杂务，但在 Stripe 的整体中，我觉得它是如此……

speaker: Unknown
en: Interesting.
zh: 有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, every business is a kind of applied theory on how some aspect of the world works or how some market works or how some, you know, if the new company with a new model, it's kind of a contrarian thesis on some counterfactual.
zh: 比如，每个企业都是一种应用理论，关于世界的某个方面如何运作、某个市场如何运作，你知道的，如果是带着新模式的新公司，它就像是对某种反事实的反主流论题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've never met a Stripe customer and thought, that's boring.
zh: 我从来没有见过一个 Stripe 客户然后想：真无聊。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's actually, the business as a whole has been the opposite of the Schlepp-Blindness instinct.
zh: 所以实际上，这个业务整体上与苦差盲的直觉恰恰相反。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you have a particularly unique perspective on this because you work with the big model providers, the big lab companies, and you work with all of the fast-growing AI startups on the ground.
zh: 而你对此有一个特别独特的视角，因为你与大型模型提供商、大型实验室公司合作，也与所有快速成长的 AI 创业公司在一线共事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Something that came up a lot here yesterday, honestly, it comes up within the batches too, is people are just worried about, is my idea going to get sort of trampled by the big lab providers?
zh: 昨天这里经常被提到的一件事，说实话，在每一批里也经常出现，就是人们只是在担心：我的想法会不会被大型实验室提供商碾压？

speaker: Unknown
en: And given your perspective, I'm just curious, how should people think about that?
zh: 鉴于你的视角，我很好奇，人们应该如何看待这个问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, again, predictions are hard, and certainly the labs are very competent, capable organizations.
zh: 是的，再说一次，预测很难，而且实验室当然是非常有能力、有实力的组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: And maybe if you separate a little bit, will rapidly improving AI capabilities do this, or will the labs specifically themselves do this?
zh: 也许可以稍微区分一下：是快速提升的 AI 能力会做到这一点，还是实验室本身特别会做到这一点？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in general, the track record of, like...
zh: 我认为总体上，这方面的履历记录是……

speaker: Unknown
en: No organization, if we go back 20 years, you know, there was some of the sense with Google, like, you know, when we were doing Octomatic, the question was always for our company and every other company, you know, what if Google does this?
zh: 没有任何组织，如果我们回到 20 年前，你知道，对 Google 有过某种类似的感觉，比如，你知道，当我们做 Octomatic 的时候，对我们公司和其他每家公司来说，问题总是：如果 Google 做了这个怎么办？

speaker: Unknown
en: And Google seemed kind of omnipotent and had this immense number of incredibly talented people and essentially infinite access to capital and servers, just all the things.
zh: 而 Google 当时似乎有点无所不能，拥有极其多才华横溢的人，以及本质上无限的资本和服务器访问权限，就是所有这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just human organizations are complicated and it's very hard to have to
zh: 而且人类组织本身就很复杂，很难做到

speaker: Unknown
en: managed to aggressively prosecute 100 different priorities and to deal with all the issues and interference that arises among them and so forth.
zh: 激进地推进 100 个不同的优先事项，并处理它们之间产生的所有问题和干扰等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, you know, Google has done incredibly well in a bunch of specific places, but it's not like Google has done all the things, even if in some kind of basic material sense, Google maybe, you know, had that ability.
zh: 所以，你知道，Google 在一堆特定领域做得非常出色，但并不是说 Google 把所有事情都做成了，即使在某种基础物质意义上，Google 也许，你知道，有那个能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'd say that kind of the track record of that is...
zh: 所以我想说，这方面的过往记录是……

speaker: Unknown
en: is checkered.
zh: 是好坏参半的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in general, I think that fear has been overstated.
zh: 总的来说，我认为这种担忧被夸大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, I think there is a more specific thing of just like models themselves.
zh: 现在，我认为有一个更具体的事情，就是模型本身。

speaker: Unknown
en: Forget the labs.
zh: 先别管那些实验室。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even if the labs aren't particularly ambitious about expanding their scope, just like literally LLMs will obviate a bunch of or agentic capabilities will obviate a bunch of
zh: 即使实验室对扩展自己的业务范围并不特别雄心勃勃，仅仅从字面上说，LLM 会取代一大堆，或者说智能体能力会取代一大堆

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, specific verticals or tasks or something.
zh: 你知道，特定的垂直领域或任务之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, hard to say.
zh: 你知道，很难说。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, contingent on one's forecast of the model capabilities themselves.
zh: 显然，这取决于一个人对模型能力本身的预测。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you know, in certain cases, I'm sure that will happen.
zh: 但你知道，在某些情况下，我确信这会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you know, in certain domains, it has already happened.
zh: 而且你知道，在某些领域，这已经发生了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Looking at the Stripe data, one thing I will say that I think is germane to people here.
zh: 看看 Stripe 的数据，有一件事我想说，我认为和在座的各位息息相关。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are many more businesses getting started now than there were a year ago, like as little as a year ago, way, way more than were getting started five years ago.
zh: 现在创办的企业比一年前多得多，就像短短一年前，比五年前多得多得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually, the relative change between last year and this year is pretty much the largest relative change we've seen in any given year.
zh: 而且实际上，去年和今年之间的相对变化，基本上是我们所见过的任何一年中最大的相对变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, for example, from 2019 to 2020, we saw a big jump.
zh: 所以，举例来说，从 2019 年到 2020 年，我们看到了一次大的跳跃。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, understandable during COVID.
zh: 你知道，这在 COVID 期间是可以理解的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in February to April of 2020 or whatever, you know, I think the growth rate inflected to maybe 50% or thereabouts year over year in terms of new businesses getting started.
zh: 所以在 2020 年 2 月到 4 月前后，你知道，我认为新创办企业的增长率拐点上扬到同比大约 50% 左右。

speaker: Unknown
en: As I speak, the number of new businesses starting on Stripe is up
zh: 就在我发言的此刻，在 Stripe 上新创办企业的数量上升了

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a bit under, but around 2x year over year, which again is the largest relative jump we've seen.
zh: 略低于但大约是同比 2 倍，这同样是我们所见过的最大的相对跳跃。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you might think, OK, fine, there's way more vibe-coded, lightweight, slop, whatever.
zh: 你可能会想，好吧，行吧，有更多 vibe coding 的、轻量的、垃圾玩意儿之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fine, there's more things, but are they actually succeeding?
zh: 行吧，东西更多了，但它们真的成功了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: But actually, the median business is doing better this year than a year ago.
zh: 但实际上，企业中位数今年比一年前做得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then if we kind of stratify it and look at the probability that any given business will reach some revenue threshold, $1 million, $5 million, $10 million, whatever, those all seem to be getting better.
zh: 然后如果我们分层来看，任何一家企业达到某个收入门槛的概率，100 万、500 万、1000 万美元之类的，这些似乎都在变好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Business are the time to revenue.
zh: 企业……到收入的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: For new companies in corporate with Atlas is declining.
zh: 对于使用 Atlas 的新公司来说正在缩短。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so by all the kind of objective metrics we can look at, it seems to be a better time than ever to start a business.
zh: 所以从我们能看到的所有客观指标来看，现在似乎是有史以来创业的最佳时机。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, again, things can change.
zh: 当然，再说一次，事情是会变的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know what the world's going to look like in five years.
zh: 我不知道五年后世界会是什么样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: But speaking today on July 26th or whatever it is of 26, I think it is...
zh: 但在今天是 26 年 7 月 26 日左右还是什么的今天发言，我认为是……

speaker: Unknown
en: The Stripe data would suggest there's never been a better time.
zh: Stripe 的数据会表明，从来没有比这更好的时机。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we see the exact same thing in the YC batches.
zh: 我是说，我们在 YC 批次里看到的就是完全一样的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: Companies are just able to grow faster than ever.
zh: 公司就是能够比以往任何时候都更快地增长。 [[268→批次内尤其如此，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Certainly within the batch, right?
zh: 当然是在批次之内，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Back in, again, the old days, when Harj and I were first starting out, getting to a million dollars of revenue, like run rate revenue, was a big deal.
zh: 回到，再说一次，过去的日子，当 Harj 和我刚起步的时候，做到 100 万美元收入，也就是 run rate 收入，是一件大事。

speaker: Unknown
en: People would know about that company.
zh: 人们会知道那家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: They'd be like, you know, I heard that X company got to a million dollars of revenue.
zh: 他们会说，你知道，我听说 X 公司做到 100 万美元收入了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now, I mean...
zh: 而现在，我是说……

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, you should be by your first month, it feels like.
zh: 是啊，感觉你第一个月就应该做到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's an exaggeration for everyone here.
zh: 对在座的各位来说这是夸张了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Certainly within the YC part of the lifecycle, like day zero to 90, it's really being driven by, I would say, enterprises willing to buy from startups, which is a new thing, so you can sign these new contracts within the batch.
zh: 当然在生命周期的 YC 阶段内，比如第 0 天到 90 天，我认为真正的驱动力是企业愿意从初创公司采购，这是一件新事物，所以你可以在批次内签下这些新合同。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have the data as the companies keep growing.
zh: 随着公司不断增长，你手上就有了数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious, are there other factors that are driving these sort of inflected growth curves from like 1 to 10 and 10 to 100?
zh: 我很好奇，还有没有其他因素在推动这种拐点上扬的增长曲线，比如从 1 到 10 和 10 到 100？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's really the dynamic you just mentioned, which is businesses everywhere are more spring-loaded to
zh: 我认为正是你刚才提到的这个动态，就是各地的企业都更加蓄势待发地

speaker: Unknown
en: adapt and to try new things.
zh: 去适应和尝试新事物。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they have a real terror of being left behind with archaic and antiquated ways of operating.
zh: 而且它们对因运营方式陈旧过时而被甩在后面有着真正的恐惧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so in normal times, you're a new startup, you have some mechanism for doing whatever, and you pitch the CIO or the CTO or the whoever at some company, and they kind of
zh: 所以在正常时期，你是一家新的初创公司，你有一套做某事的机制，你去向某家公司的 CIO 或 CTO 或 whoever 做推介，然后他们有点……

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't want to talk to you because your thing is not validated.
zh: 不想跟你谈，因为你的东西还没得到验证。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe you won't be around in two years.
zh: 也许两年后你就不在了。

speaker: Unknown
en: All the kind of obvious objections.
zh: 所有那些显而易见的反对意见。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now people know that, well, the risk of the status quo is actually extremely high.
zh: 但现在人们知道，维持现状的风险实际上极高。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so even if there's risk in doing all the new things, well,
zh: 所以即使做所有这些新事情也有风险，嗯，

speaker: Unknown
en: This path also looks pretty dangerous.
zh: 这条老路看起来也相当危险。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I really think there's never been a better time for startups to sell and to have their products get adopted at a pretty meaningful scale right out of the gate.
zh: 所以我真的认为，对于初创公司来说，从来没有比现在更好的时机去销售，并让自己的产品从一开始就获得相当有规模的采用。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of YC companies in recent times have demonstrated this.
zh: 近来很多 YC 公司已经证明了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think it's a really pervasive dynamic.
zh: 但我认为这是一个非常普遍的动态。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a bit of it, I think, also.
zh: 而且我认为还有一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, Stripe is not a consumer company, obviously.
zh: 我是说，Stripe 显然不是一家消费公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think there's some version of this on the consumer side where I think consumers are also pretty, I mean,
zh: 但我认为在消费端也存在某种类似的版本，我觉得消费者也相当，我是说，

speaker: Unknown
en: Consumers have complicated views on AI, and maybe they don't want the data centers, but people are very intrigued by the product, and I think they're kind of beguiled by them, and there's a predisposition and an openness to experimenting with the new.
zh: 消费者对 AI 有着复杂的看法，也许他们不想要数据中心，但人们对这些产品非常感兴趣，而且我觉得他们有点被这些产品迷住了，存在一种尝试新事物的倾向和开放心态。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe just more broadly, something I'm curious about is, again, with the data you have at Stripe, has anything you've seen in that data changed a belief you have about AI broadly, say, over the last 12 months?
zh: 更宽泛地说，我好奇的一点是，还是基于你在 Stripe 掌握的数据，在过去 12 个月左右，你在这些数据中看到的任何东西有没有改变你对 AI 的整体看法？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, there's a fear that AI is going to be this hegemonic, centralizing, totalizing force where a small number of companies gobble up a very large share of the economy.
zh: 我是说，存在一种担忧，即 AI 会成为一种霸权的、中心化的、总体化的力量，少数几家公司会吞掉经济中非常大的份额。

speaker: Unknown
en: Many companies at the forefront of AI have done incredibly well and I think will continue to do incredibly well for sure.
zh: 许多处于 AI 前沿的公司已经做得极其出色，而且我相信它们肯定会继续做得极其出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: But basically we can see at Stripe the hunger and the intensity with which other companies are either getting started taking advantage of these new capabilities or existing companies are retooling.
zh: 但基本上我们在 Stripe 可以看到，其他公司要么是初创公司利用这些新能力、要么是现有公司在进行改造，其渴望和力度有多强。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't worry about the centralization in the same way.
zh: 我不再以同样的方式担心中心化问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there are going to be many thousands of winners.
zh: 我认为将会出现成千上万个赢家。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, we try not to offer any definitive prognostications because the future is not predetermined.
zh: 再说一次，我们尽量不给出任何确定性的预测，因为未来不是预先注定的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But based on the trend lines we can see, I think we are heading towards a more decentralized world and one with more broad-based prosperity.
zh: 但根据我们能看到趋势线，我认为我们正走向一个更加去中心化的世界，一个拥有更广泛繁荣的世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I think that is all we have time for today.
zh: 嗯，我想今天我们的时间就到这里了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So thanks so much, Patrick, for being here.
zh: 非常感谢 Patrick 来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for having me.
zh: 谢谢你们的邀请。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it would be remiss of me not to say that Stripe would not exist without YC.
zh: 如果我不说一句“没有 YC 就没有 Stripe”的话，那就是我的失职了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, cool.
zh: 哦，好。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much.
zh: 非常感谢。
